171: The din of the issur of accepting rechiluth obtains even when he speaks 'in his innocence." That is, when he [the hearer] sees that the speaker did not intend to stir up strife against his friend, but that it [the rechiluth] left his mouth by chance. (All of its other details are explained above in Part One, Principle VII, section 9, in respect to lashon hara. The same applies to rechiluth.)
